title: Torsion and the PBC property
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a discrete commutative ring, with the coefficient conventions of [sk-def-pbc-conventions]. Sheaves are on the small étale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]; a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules means a sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

A sheaf $F$ of abelian groups, or of $\Lambda$-modules, is *torsion* if every
geometric stalk is a torsion abelian group. Equivalently,

$$
F=\varinjlim_{n\geq1}F[n],\qquad F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F),
$$

where the positive integers are ordered by divisibility. These are sheaf
colimits. The equivalence follows by taking geometric stalks, which commute
with colimits and finite limits and detect isomorphisms.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$, write $\mathrm{PBC}_\Lambda(f)$ if the exchange
morphism $\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ of [sk-def-exchange]
is an isomorphism in $D^+(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ for every base change
$g:Y'\to Y$ and every $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ with torsion cohomology
sheaves. Put $\mathrm{PBC}(f)=\mathrm{PBC}_{\mathbf Z}(f)$. The definition
makes sense for any $f$; for proper $f$ (in the sense of [sk-def-conv]) the property is proved in
the blueprint units sk-thm-p1 and sk-thm-reduction.

Torsion is a local condition on sections: every section is killed by an
integer after an étale covering, with the integer allowed to vary between
members of the covering. On a non-quasi-compact object a section need not be
killed by a single integer. For example, the constant sheaf $\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z$
on a nonempty scheme is torsion, but on the disjoint union of countably many
copies of the scheme its sections include $(1/2^n)_{n\geq1}$, which has
infinite order.

proof.text: For an abelian sheaf $F$, use the kernel and colimit construction of [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Explicitly, if $n\mid m$ and $ns=0$, then $ms=(m/n)(ns)=0$, so the kernel inclusions form a diagram indexed by positive integers under divisibility. This is a small filtered category: it contains $1$, and $nm$ is an upper bound for $n,m$; parallel arrows in a poset already agree. The compatible inclusions give the specified comparison $c_F:\varinjlim_n F[n]\to F$. Thus the displayed equality means that this canonical comparison is an isomorphism, not a sectionwise colimit assertion.

source.place: first paragraph and displayed torsion-kernel colimit

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations], conditions (1), (2), (3), to this very $c_F$: it is an isomorphism exactly when all geometric stalks are torsion, and exactly when every section is locally killed by positive integers with locally varying orders. The stalk explanation in the source uses precisely [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits], and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]: the stalk of $c_F$ is the inclusion of the union of the subgroups killed by $n$ into $F_{\bar t}$, which is surjective exactly when that group is torsion. An exact additive stalk functor also preserves finite products (finite biproducts) and kernels, hence finite limits. No quasi-compactness hypothesis is used.

source.place: first paragraph, equivalence and sentence explaining the geometric-stalk argument; last paragraph, local condition

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules, work with module-valued sheaves using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-constant-ring-equivalence], which retains the underlying abelian sheaf $A$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], kernels are sectionwise, so the underlying sheaf of $F[n]$ is $A[n]$, with the same inclusions. Apply parts (2) and (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to the small divisibility diagram: its module-sheaf colimit exists, and forgetting modules carries its colimit cocone to the abelian colimit cocone, so it carries $c_F$ to $c_A$. The required abelian sheafification exists on the small étale site, as included in that node's hypotheses and example. If the underlying abelian-sheaf map is invertible, its inverse commutes with restrictions. At every object $U$ it is linear over the scalar ring: applying the injective map $c_F(U)$ to $c_F(U)^{-1}(a y)$ and to $a c_F(U)^{-1}(y)$ gives $a y$ in both cases. Thus this inverse is a module-sheaf morphism, so forgetting reflects isomorphisms. The underlying abelian geometric stalk is likewise the stalk of $A$: in the pointed-neighbourhood description [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], forgetting changes neither representatives $(U,\bar u,s)$ nor their restriction identifications; addition and scalar multiplication are induced on these same germ classes. Consequently torsion of these stalks and local annihilation of sections are exactly the conditions of step 2 for $A$. This proves all torsion characterizations for $\Lambda$-module sheaves as well.

source.place: first paragraph, words "or of Lambda-modules", and sheaf-colimit convention

proof.text: For any morphism $f:X\to Y$, use $D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and its cohomology sheaves from [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Require each $\mathcal H^j(K)$ to satisfy the torsion condition of steps 2 and 3. For every $g:Y'\to Y$ and its cartesian square, the specified adjunction construction of [sk-def-exchange] supplies $\Ex_{\square,K}:g^{-1}Rf_*K\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$ in $D^+(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The conjunction of the assertions that these specified arrows are isomorphisms is the definition of $\mathrm{PBC}_\Lambda(f)$. Substitute $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ to define $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$. This formation uses no properness assumption or invertibility of torsion orders; the subsequent properness theorem is a forward reference, not a premise of this definition. In particular this definition quantifies over complexes with torsion cohomology, rather than only degree-zero sheaves.

source.place: second paragraph, definition of PBC_Lambda(f) and its specialization to Z

proof.text: For the final example apply the moreover clause of [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] with $T$ nonempty. It states that $\underline{\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z}$ is torsion and that restriction from $U=\coprod_{n\ge1}T$ identifies its sections with the product of the sections on the copies of $T$, where the section with constant dyadic coordinates has infinite order. Thus the phrase $(1/2^n)_{n\ge1}$ means the glued section with coordinates given by the canonical constant-sheaf maps; it is not an assertion that all sections on $T$ are constant. This gives the claimed failure of a single global annihilator while retaining local annihilators.

source.place: last paragraph, non-quasi-compact object and constant Q/Z example

proof_origin.place: first two paragraphs: torsion definition and canonical torsion-kernel colimit; PBC definition; last paragraph: local torsion and the dyadic counterexample
